clusters.title: SSTF seek-time/head-movement on a request queue
clusters.technique: Sort out nearest-first order: from the head repeatedly pick the pending request with smallest |difference|; add the gaps (multiply by ms per cylinder if asked). Draw the visiting order on one line.
clusters.what_changes: Request list, head start, cylinder count and ms/cylinder. june2019_q41 and june2023_q78 are the same queue (4,34,10,7,19,73,2,15,6,20 from 50 = 119).
clusters.skip_note: If you can run SSTF once on june2023_q78 the other three are only different numbers.

clusters.title: Total head movement for FCFS / SCAN / C-SCAN / C-LOOK
clusters.technique: FCFS = sum of consecutive gaps. SCAN goes to the disk end then reverses; C-SCAN goes to the end then jumps to 0 (jump counted in the usual textbook answer) and continues; LOOK/C-LOOK turn at the last request, not the disk end.
clusters.what_changes: Algorithm, direction, start head, queue, disk size.
clusters.skip_note: Same single skill of tracing one policy; after solving the June 2025 queue under two policies the rest follow.

clusters.title: Identify the 2nd request served / the policy from a head graph
clusters.technique: Trace the policy order on the same queue: C-LOOK(right) serves increasing requests then jumps to the lowest; SCAN(left) serves decreasing requests first. For a graph, look for a jump back without touching the disk end = C-LOOK.
clusters.what_changes: Which policy and direction; asks order rather than total.
clusters.skip_note: Pure order-of-service tracing already trained by the head-movement cluster.

clusters.title: Disk capacity / geometry arithmetic
clusters.technique: capacity = surfaces x tracks x sectors/track x bytes/sector; cylinders = tracks per surface; sector-address bits = log2(total sectors).
clusters.what_changes: Which quantity is asked (capacity, track size, bits, sectors per track).
clusters.skip_note: All are multiplications of the same four parameters; do nov2020_q92 and the rest are the same product.

clusters.title: Rotational delay and data-transfer rate
clusters.technique: max rotational delay = 60/rpm s (avg = half); transfer rate = bytes per track x revolutions per second.
clusters.what_changes: rpm and which of the two is asked.
clusters.skip_note: Both come from the nov2020 passage disk; one rep suffices.

clusters.title: RAID level matching
clusters.technique: Memorise: 0 striping, 1 mirroring, 2 bit-level ECC (memory-style), 3 bit-interleaved parity, 4 block-interleaved parity, 5 block-interleaved distributed parity, 6 P+Q / Reed-Solomon.
clusters.what_changes: Pairing of levels with descriptions; wording of descriptions varies.
clusters.skip_note: Same table of RAID facts every time; learn it once.

clusters.title: File allocation methods and fragmentation
clusters.technique: Contiguous: external fragmentation, fast direct access. Linked: no external fragmentation, no direct access, pointer space. Indexed: direct + sequential, no external fragmentation, index-block overhead.
clusters.what_changes: Direction of question (which suffers / which advantages).

clusters.title: Paging address arithmetic (pages, frames, offset, page table size, internal fragmentation)
clusters.technique: pages = VA size/page size; offset bits = log2(page size); frames = PM size/page size; PT size = pages x entry size; internal fragmentation = unused part of last page.
clusters.what_changes: Memory sizes, page size, PTE size, which quantity asked.
clusters.skip_note: Nov 2021 passage gives all subparts; rest are variants of the same computation.

clusters.title: Effective access time with TLB
clusters.technique: EMAT = h(t+m) + (1-h)(t+2m) for single-level paging (t = TLB time, m = memory time).

clusters.title: Logical / virtual / physical address terminology
clusters.technique: Address in main memory = physical address; CPU-generated = logical (virtual); address space = logical/virtual set, memory space = physical set.

clusters.title: Count page faults on a reference string (FIFO / LRU / Optimal)
clusters.technique: Simulate frames in a table; FIFO evicts oldest loaded, LRU least recently used, Optimal the page used farthest in future. Count misses.
clusters.what_changes: Algorithm, frame count and reference string (and sometimes a difference between two algorithms).
clusters.skip_note: Mechanical simulation; practise on nov2020_q15 (FIFO and LRU) and the others are the same drill.

clusters.title: June 2023 passage: column-major vs row-major array traversal under LRU
clusters.technique: Pages hold rows of 1024 entries per page; column-wise traversal of 17 rows with 17 or fewer frames: count faults per column vs row-wise: 17 faults once, then hits.
clusters.what_changes: Subquestion (faults, hit ratio, ratio of faults).
clusters.skip_note: One passage; solving one sub-question gives all.

clusters.title: Effective access time with page faults / hit ratio
clusters.technique: EAT = (1-p)*m + p*(fault service time); with hit ratio h: h*t_primary + (1-h)*t_secondary.

clusters.title: Virtual memory conceptual statements
clusters.technique: Virtual memory increases effective capacity; program can be larger than RAM; not all pages need to be loaded; address translation for every logical address.

clusters.title: Order of page-replacement steps
clusters.technique: Find page on disk; if no free frame use algorithm to pick victim, write it back if dirty, update tables; read in desired page; restart instruction.

clusters.title: Linux interrupt protection level ordering
clusters.technique: Increasing priority: user mode < kernel system service routines < bottom half handlers < top half handlers.
clusters.what_changes: Only the lettering of the options.
clusters.skip_note: Identical question in Dec 2023 and June 2025.

clusters.title: I/O protection and interrupts
clusters.technique: I/O instructions are privileged; with memory-mapped I/O protection is by the OS (memory protection); I/O completion interrupts are different from a trap for protection.

clusters.title: Unix/Linux command facts
clusters.technique: wc -l counts lines; chmod -R a+x; lpr prints; user passwords/accounts in /etc/passwd; glob *.[ch].

clusters.title: Process-creation system calls (fork, exec, clone, kill, exit)
clusters.technique: fork creates child; exec loads new program; kill sends signal; exit terminates; clone gives selective sharing flags (Linux).

clusters.title: Match-the-following of OS terms
clusters.technique: Link each term to its area: Banker = resource allocation, demand paging = virtual memory, LFU = cache replacement, critical section = mutual exclusion, firmware = ROM, PCB = TCB, IPC = computational speedup.
clusters.skip_note: Examiner reuses the same standard pairings.

clusters.title: Preemptive SJF / SRTF waiting or turnaround time
clusters.technique: Draw the Gantt chart; at every arrival compare remaining times. TAT = CT - AT; WT = TAT - BT.
clusters.what_changes: Arrival and burst values; nov2021_q75 and july2018_q59 are near-identical sets.

clusters.title: Non-preemptive FCFS / SJF / HRRN metrics on one process set
clusters.technique: FCFS by arrival; SJF picks the smallest burst among arrived processes; HRRN ratio = (W+S)/S. Weighted turnaround = TAT/burst.
clusters.skip_note: Dec 2024 passage shares one table across sub-questions.

clusters.title: Priority scheduling average waiting / response time (non-preemptive)
clusters.technique: Order by priority (lower number first), then cumulative start times give waiting times.

clusters.title: Round-robin waiting/turnaround and maximum wait
clusters.technique: Simulate the queue with quantum q; waiting = completion - arrival - burst; worst-case wait for n processes = (n-1)q.

clusters.title: Scheduling theory statements (starvation, response time, quantum)
clusters.technique: SRTF and priority may starve; HRRN/aging fixes starvation; RR gives better response than FCFS; tiny quantum means many context switches.

clusters.title: Preemptive vs non-preemptive circumstances
clusters.technique: Preemption happens when running->ready or waiting->ready; non-preemptive SJF never context-switches mid-burst.

clusters.title: Thread concepts and models
clusters.technique: Threads share code, data and files but have own stack and registers; user library creates threads; concurrency one-to-one > many-to-many > many-to-one.

clusters.title: Process model basics (states, queue, PCB, heap, cascading termination)
clusters.technique: Running can go to ready (timer), waiting (I/O); ready queue holds ready processes in memory; PCB holds state, registers, scheduling info (not code); heap = dynamic memory; cascading termination.

clusters.title: OS-specific scheduling (Windows, Linux)
clusters.technique: Windows 16 non-real-time priorities (and 16 real-time); Linux supports preemptive priority and time-sharing.

clusters.title: Counting semaphore value after P and V operations
clusters.technique: final = initial - (#P) + (#V).
clusters.what_changes: Which of the three quantities is unknown.

clusters.title: Mutual exclusion and critical-section statements
clusters.technique: Only one process in critical section; structure entry/critical/exit/remainder; spin lock = busy waiting; unaware processes still have mutual exclusion, starvation, deadlock problems but not coherence.

clusters.title: Maximum processes for deadlock freedom
clusters.technique: Deadlock-free if R >= n(m-1)+1, so n_max = floor((R-1)/(m-1)).

clusters.title: Banker's algorithm passage
clusters.technique: Banker avoids deadlock; needs Max, Allocation, Available matrices/vectors; grants only if the system stays in a safe state.

clusters.title: Symbol table
clusters.technique: Symbol table used for storage allocation, type checking, duplicate-error suppression; hash table gives fastest access.

clusters.title: Compiler phases order and roles
clusters.technique: Lexical -> syntax -> semantic -> intermediate code -> optimization -> code generation; syntax analysis checks grammar.

examiner_mindset: Numerical questions (scheduling, disk scheduling, page-fault counting, paging arithmetic, semaphore arithmetic) form roughly a third of the unit; small data sets, always solvable by hand.
Same data is reused: june2019_q41 and june2023_q78 share one SSTF queue, nov2021_q75 and july2018_q59 share a preemptive SJF set, dec2023_q80 and june2025_q30 are the same question.

Passage-based multi-question sets (nov2020 disk, nov2021 paging, june2023 LRU array, june2024 Banker, dec2024 scheduling, june2025 disk queue) give 5 questions each and are the main source of repetition.
Match-the-following questions mix terms across OS areas; the same standard pairings recur (RAID levels, Banker = resource allocation).
Trap options: C-SCAN/SCAN differences (jump counted or not), the difference between FIFO and LRU for Belady, 'current needs' column in Banker.
Distractors are near-values from off-by-one or unit mistakes (KB vs bytes, ms vs seconds).
Difficulty is mostly easy to moderate; heavy theory such as formal proofs or code is never asked, but fork-counting appears occasionally.
Cross-unit overlap: Unit 5 questions on OS appear in matching with data structures and networking cloud terms; compiler and assembler items are minor.
Process management and file systems/disk scheduling alone take over 40% of the unit.
Never asked: kernel source code, detailed Windows internals beyond priority counts, deep distributed OS theory.

formulas.name: Deadlock-free process bound
formulas.formula: R >= n(m-1)+1, so n_max = floor((R-1)/(m-1))
formulas.note: R resources, each process needs m; e.g. R=12,m=4 gives 3

formulas.name: Banker: Need
formulas.formula: Need = Max - Allocation; safe if some order lets every process finish with Available
formulas.note: In dec2019_q28 'Current needs' column is actually the allocation

formulas.name: Disk capacity
formulas.formula: surfaces x tracks per surface x sectors per track x bytes per sector

formulas.name: Sector-address bits
formulas.formula: log2(surfaces x tracks x sectors)

formulas.name: Rotational delay
formulas.formula: max = 60/rpm seconds; average = half of that

formulas.name: Data transfer rate
formulas.formula: bytes per track x revolutions per second

formulas.name: Seek time
formulas.formula: total head movement x time per cylinder
formulas.note: SSTF picks nearest pending request each time

formulas.name: Disk policies
formulas.formula: SCAN goes to end then reverses; C-SCAN goes to end then jumps to start; LOOK/C-LOOK turn at the last request
formulas.note: C-SCAN return jump counted in textbook answers

formulas.name: Inode maximum file size
formulas.formula: (direct + p + p^2) x block size, p = block size/address size

formulas.name: Tape write time
formulas.formula: (data / recording density) / speed (+ inter-block gaps)

formulas.name: Paging sizes
formulas.formula: pages = VA/page size; offset bits = log2(page); frames = PM/page; page table size = pages x entry size

formulas.name: Internal fragmentation
formulas.formula: unused space in last page = pages x page size - process size
formulas.note: 34 KB with 4 KB pages gives 2 KB

formulas.name: EMAT with TLB
formulas.note: Single level page table; two-level adds extra m

formulas.name: EAT with page faults
formulas.formula: (1-p)m + p x fault time; or p + q/100 if one fault per 100

formulas.name: Swap time
formulas.formula: 2 x (size/transfer rate) + latencies

formulas.name: Belady's anomaly
formulas.formula: Occurs for FIFO; LRU and optimal are stack algorithms and have no anomaly

formulas.name: Little's law
formulas.formula: n = lambda x W

formulas.name: Scheduling times
formulas.formula: TAT = CT - AT; WT = TAT - BT; RT = first run - AT; HRRN ratio = (W+S)/S

formulas.name: RR worst-case wait
formulas.formula: (n-1) x q

formulas.name: Counting semaphore
formulas.formula: final = initial - #P + #V

formulas.name: fork count
formulas.formula: k sequential forks create 2^k processes
formulas.note: Count prints by tracing each fork

formulas.name: RAID levels
formulas.formula: 0 striping,1 mirror,2 bit ECC,3 bit parity,4 block parity,5 distributed block parity,6 P+Q

formulas.name: Linux interrupt priority
formulas.formula: user < kernel system service < bottom half < top half

formulas.name: Thread sharing
formulas.formula: Shared: code,data,files,address space. Private: stack,registers,PC
formulas.note: Threads of same process share address space

formulas.name: Thread model concurrency
formulas.formula: one-to-one > many-to-many > many-to-one
formulas.note: Many-to-one blocks entirely on a blocking call

formulas.name: Boot order
formulas.formula: ROM firmware -> boot block -> bootstrap loader -> kernel

formulas.name: Layered file system
formulas.formula: Application -> logical FS -> file organization module -> basic FS -> I/O control

formulas.name: File allocation
formulas.formula: Contiguous has external fragmentation; linked and indexed do not

formulas.name: Compiler phase order
formulas.formula: lexical, syntax, semantic, intermediate code, optimization, code generation
formulas.note: Hash table best for symbol table

formulas.name: Unix facts
formulas.formula: fork creates child; exec loads program; kill signals; clone selective sharing; wc -l; lpr; /etc/passwd; chmod -R a+x
